manager_rule: Maintain a session-scoped boolean flag 'absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed'. After each round R: compute inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected = unconnected[R] minus (count of distinct Kelvin member net names appearing in failing_reasons[R] with 'has unconnected ratlines'). If ALL of the following hold simultaneously: (a) inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected >= 1, AND (b) absorbed + trimmed_spurs + removed_orphans >= n_stubs AND n_stubs > 0 (total elimination this round), AND (c) kelvin_unrouted > 0 in round R's result, AND (d) the compiler's nets list is non-empty: then (1) set absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed = True; (2) do NOT increment net_absorption_count for any net in round R's compiler nets list — the absorption verdict for those nets is suspect and should not accumulate toward Rules 37/38/39 thresholds; (3) for the immediately following round R+1, allow stubs produced by the compiler for every net that appeared in round R's compiler nets list to pass through the absorber, spur-trimmer, and orphan-removal stages without elimination (treat those stubs as exempt from absorption for round R+1 only, in the same manner as mandatory_kelvin_bypass for absorber purposes — this exemption does NOT affect compiler_excluded_nets or force-injection for Kelvin nets); (4) log 'absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed' with fields: (a) round R, (b) compiler nets list, (c) inferred_non_kelvin_unconnected count, (d) absorbed/trimmed_spurs/removed_orphans/n_stubs values, (e) confirmation that net_absorption_count was not incremented for listed nets, (f) confirmation absorber bypass is active for those nets in R+1; (5) reset absorber_false_positive_bypass_armed = False immediately after round R+1 is dispatched. This rule is additive to Rules 37, 38, 39, 40, 41, 43, 44, and 45; it does not replace or defer any action those rules independently mandate, and in rounds where Rule 41 also fires (zero-overlap + total elimination), both protocols apply concurrently — Rule 41 bypasses absorber for ALL R+1 stubs while this rule additionally suppresses R's net_absorption_count increments. Rationale: when the absorber eliminates all compiler stubs (marking target nets as fully routed) yet DRC reports more unconnected ratlines than Kelvin failures alone account for, at least one absorbed stub targeted a net that FR failed to fully route in the current candidate — a false positive where historical routing state diverges from current connectivity. Bypassing the absorber for those specific nets in R+1 gives FR routing guidance for nets it did not complete. Suppressing the net_absorption_count increment prevents the false-positive absorption from incorrectly advancing those nets toward the fast-track exclusion threshold in Rules 37/38/39, which would eventually exclude from the compiler nets that still genuinely need routing guidance.
